macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades mixed near $63K as ETF flows and macro signals drive sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported around the low-$63,000 range over the last day, with several market recaps showing small moves rather than a decisive breakout. One recap said BTC was up 0.84% in 24 hours, while other market feeds showed BTC slightly lower or broadly flat, highlighting a choppy market backdrop.

items.title: Ethereum, XRP and Solana mostly flat as crypto market stays rangebound
items.summary: Recent market updates showed ETH, XRP and SOL moving little over 24 hours, suggesting traders were waiting for a clearer catalyst. One market snapshot reported BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL and DOGE all near unchanged on the day.

items.title: Arbitrum surges after Robinhood Chain activity boosts onchain trading volumes
items.summary: ARB jumped sharply after Robinhood Chain, built on Arbitrum’s technology stack, reportedly logged $568 million in daily trading volume. The move was framed as a notable project-development story for Ethereum scaling and DeFi infrastructure.

items.title: XRP gains after SWIFT-linked blockchain payments headlines
items.summary: XRP was among the tokens getting attention after reports that SWIFT tapped Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments. The story added to ongoing speculation around enterprise blockchain adoption and cross-border settlement use cases.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong’s SFC reportedly forced crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, a move aimed at improving account security and reducing takeover risk. The development adds to the region’s active regulatory oversight of digital-asset platforms.

items.title: Canada advances stablecoin framework as broader payment modernization continues
items.summary: Canadian authorities were reported to be considering stablecoin rules, with Scotiabank saying the initiative is more about modernizing payments than reshaping wider financial markets. The policy direction points to continued regulatory normalization rather than a crackdown.

items.title: Singapore expands Ripple-related approvals for wider XRP and RLUSD services
items.summary: Ripple said it can now offer broader XRP and RLUSD services after receiving approval from Singapore regulators. The move is a notable licensing milestone for the company’s regulated payments and stablecoin business in Asia.

items.title: Europe seizes $1.51B crypto-mixing service in major anti-laundering action
items.summary: European authorities dismantled Cryptomixer, a bitcoin-mixing service they said was used by ransomware groups and darknet markets, and seized servers, data and about $29 million in BTC. The action is one of the largest recent enforcement moves tied to crypto laundering infrastructure.

items.title: Bitcoin selloff deepens amid broad market weakness
items.summary: Multiple market recaps described BTC as falling roughly 1% to nearly 6% depending on the time snapshot, with broader crypto indices also down. CoinDesk’s latest updates linked the decline to a wider risk-off move across digital assets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google delays Gemini 3.5 Pro after internal testing falls short
items.summary: DX Today reports that Google has delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro because internal testing did not meet expectations, a development that reportedly weighed on Alphabet shares. The same roundup frames this as one of the biggest AI product updates in the last day.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Image, its first image generation model
items.summary: AI Base says Meta has released Muse Image, described as Meta’s first image generation model, and made it available across Meta AI, Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, Messenger, and Advantage+ Ads. If accurate, this is one of the most notable consumer-facing model launches in the past 24 hours.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly gets approval for GPT-5.6 public deployment
items.summary: AI Base reports that the U.S. Commerce Department lifted restrictions on OpenAI’s GPT-5.6, clearing the way for broad public release. The same report says OpenAI plans to launch GPT-5.6 Sol alongside two new models, Terra and Luna.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice model
items.summary: AI Weekly says OpenAI released GPT-Live, a voice model that can listen and speak simultaneously, and that it is rolling out to Free, Go, Plus, and Pro users. This appears to be one of the day’s most significant product announcements in voice AI.

items.title: NVIDIA launches Nemotron-Labs-Audex-30B-A3B for unified audio intelligence
items.summary: AI Base reports that NVIDIA introduced a new unified audio-text model, Nemotron-Labs-Audex-30B-A3B, aimed at improving audio understanding while preserving text reasoning quality. The report says it uses a single Transformer and a mixture-of-experts design.

items.title: Meta’s Superintelligence Labs ships first image model ‘Muse Image’ across its apps
items.summary: AI Weekly separately reports that Meta’s Superintelligence Labs has shipped its first image model, Muse Image, with broad rollout across Meta’s consumer platforms. This reinforces that Meta’s newest image-generation push is a key industry development today.

items.title: Wimbledon expands IBM AI tools for live match coverage
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence News reports that Wimbledon is adding IBM-built AI features to its app and website for live match updates, contextual responses, and explanations of plays. This is a notable example of AI adoption in sports media and fan engagement.

items.title: Google folds Display Ads into AI-first Demand Gen platform
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence News says Google is moving Display Ads into its AI-powered Demand Gen platform, signaling a major shift in Google’s advertising stack. The change suggests continued reorganization of ad products around AI-driven automation.

items.title: Takeda signs up to US$600 million AI drug discovery deal with Insilico
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence News reports that Takeda entered a deal worth up to US$600 million to use Insilico Medicine’s Pharma.AI platform for early-stage drug discovery. The agreement highlights continued momentum for AI in pharmaceuticals.

items.title: China launches 29-nation AI cooperation body
items.summary: DX Today reports that China launched a 29-nation AI cooperation body, which it frames as part of Beijing’s push for global AI collaboration and influence. This is a major policy and industry-development story from the past day.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass July lineup, plus major new game announcements
items.summary: Microsoft has unveiled the next wave of Xbox Game Pass additions, while recent showcase coverage also highlighted new reveals such as Grasshopper Manufacture’s sci-fi action game and a surprise Helldivers 2 Warbond. These are among the most visible release and announcement stories from the last day of gaming coverage.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 1 sales set to end in Europe in 2027
items.summary: Nintendo will stop selling the original Switch, Switch Lite, and Switch OLED in Europe next year, according to recent reporting. The move is tied to changes in EU battery regulations and marks a major hardware lifecycle shift.

items.title: Subnautica 2 surpasses 5 million copies sold
items.summary: The sequel has crossed 5 million sales, making it one of the standout recent commercial success stories in games. The milestone was reported within the past day of gaming industry updates.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 sales top 1 million copies
items.summary: 11 bit studios’ Frostpunk 2 has reportedly sold more than 1 million copies. The figure is one of the clearest recent indicators of strong demand in the premium PC strategy market.

items.title: Epic settles dispute with Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games has reached a settlement with a former contractor accused of leaking information about Fortnite collaborations. The case is a notable recent industry/legal development around leaks and content security.

items.title: WayForward announces next Shantae game
items.summary: WayForward revealed the next Shantae title at Anime Expo and gave it a 2027 release window. The announcement is one of the more notable upcoming game reveals in recent coverage.

items.title: IO confirms Project Fantasy will continue independently after Xbox split
items.summary: IO has said Project Fantasy will continue after the company’s split from Xbox. The update is part of a broader wave of industry restructuring and platform strategy changes.

items.title: Bethesda boss says studio will restructure around its strongest franchises after cuts
items.summary: Bethesda leadership reportedly told staff it will reorganize around its strongest franchises following cuts. The comments reflect continuing layoffs and consolidation across major publishers.

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly scales down new Ghost Recon project amid layoffs
items.summary: Recent reports say Ubisoft has reduced the scope of the next Ghost Recon and cut some developers working on it. The story adds to the broader trend of AAA project resets and workforce reductions.

items.title: Build a Rocket Boy employees plan protest over upcoming fan event
items.summary: Employees at Build a Rocket Boy are reportedly preparing to protest an all-expenses-paid fan event. The situation highlights labor tensions surrounding live game promotion and studio operations.
